chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil told us, he said: Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari told us, he said: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told us, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Jamil ibn Salih, from al-Walid ibn al-Abbas, he said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say:
Nobility is good deeds, honor is wealth, and dignity is God-consciousness.

key_terms.الْحَسَبُ: Nobility or lineage, often contrasted with action in this context
key_terms.الْفِعَالُ: Deeds or actions, specifically good deeds here
key_terms.الْكَرَمُ: Generosity, dignity, or nobility of character

ai.seo_question: What is the true source of nobility and dignity in Shia Islam according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this concise maxim from *Ma'ani al-Akhbar*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) redefines social stratification by prioritizing ethical conduct over genealogy, linking material honor to wealth, and anchoring ultimate dignity in *taqwa*. This triad reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the transformation of pre-Islamic tribal values into a meritocratic spiritual framework, where inner piety supersedes external status. The statement serves as a practical guide for evaluating personal worth within the community, balancing worldly realities with divine consciousness.

en.basel-kadem: 74. We were told by Muhammed bin Musa ibn Mutawakkil, that he said: We were told by Abdullah bin Ja’far al-Himyari, that he said: We were told by Muhammed bin Hussain, from Hasan bin Mahbub, from Jameel bin Saleh, from Waleed bin Abbas, that he said: I heard Abu Abdillah (a.s) say:
“Nobility is good act. Honor is (possession of) property. Dignity is godfearness.”
